About the 100 KB limit

100 KB is the usual advice for images on a web page: small enough not to hurt your Largest Contentful Paint, large enough to still look right on a retina screen.

It binary-searches the JPEG quality setting and keeps the largest file that still fits under 100 KB — the biggest file under a ceiling is the best-looking one. If even low quality is too big it scales the image down in steps and searches again, and tells you so.
It is a good default for a content image. Hero images can justify more, thumbnails far less. If page speed is the goal, WebP at the same visual quality is smaller again.
No. The work happens in this tab using Canvas. Your image never touches a server, which is also why it keeps working with no network once the page has loaded.
